title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Profaned Capital -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : The Profaned Capital was ruled over by Yhorm the Giant, descendant of an ancient conqueror, who was nevertheless asked by the previously subjugated people to lead them. A sorcery school was established there, one of two leading schools claiming to be heir to the legacy of Big Hat Logan. The court sorcerers from the Profaned Capital also served as priests, as golden stitching of their robes suggest. Although they were undeniably intelligent and adept in their craft, it is possible that they did not follow Big Hat Logan as much as they claimed to. Despite the Citizens of the Profaned Capital called Yhorm "King", their hearts were not their voice, meaning they merely used him and didn't trust him.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Profaned Capital -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Profaned Capital is a highly decimated ruin that has somehow sunken into a great chasm, the only natural light pouring from a crack in the cavernous walls. Very little of what was once a proud civilization remains, making this area quite small. The state of the Capital is in such disarray that the only things remaining are a few bridges and tunnels, a vestige of a great tower, a church sunken in a swamp, and the throne room of Yhorm the Giant. The rest of what was once a prosperous realm has long since corroded away. An overlook of the Capital is viewable from Irithyll Dungeon.

One of two bonfires is within the central tower, its interior hollowed out, but its heights traversable thanks to numerous ladders up and down its interior and exterior. The source of the ladders is no mystery, as the corpse of Laddersmith Gilligan can be seen splayed out right by the bonfire, where the player can learn a gesture.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Yhorm refused to serve as fuel for the First Flame a second time due to the fact that, once awakened from his grave, he realized that his sacrifice had been futile. The sorcerers of the Profaned Capital had continued to experiment on the Profaned Flame he had tried to quell with his sacrifice and as a result the entire city was destroyed, making his life of service meaningless even after the end. The moment he rises from the grave, he can be seen already howling in despair. In addition, he may also have simply understood the state of the world, now corrupted beyond any possibility of traditional salvation through the linking of the Fire, and simply decided to await death in the ruins of his city.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Yhorm defended the kingdom from many threats, serving as the kingdom's heavy blade and solid shield, and at some point, Yhorm acquired two Storm Rulers, probably from the enemies he defeated. He gave one such sword to his subjects in an efford to win their trust.

As a result of a curse which bound a group of women which were four relatives of a priest (a court sorcerer), the everlasting Profaned Flame was triggered. Those involved in the curse went on living carelessly, although the curse turned the women into malformed creatures.. The sorcerers created Gargoyles that wield either spears, or hammers imbued with the Profaned Flame.

After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

The only survivors of the Capital are the Handmaids, the court sorcerer Eamon, and the four malformed women. The Handmaids who served in the Capital reportedly took pleasure in hurting others.

Sometime after the Profaned Flame destroyed the Capital, Pontiff Sulyvahn discovered the Profaned Flame and the Capital, "a burning ambition took root within him". He would later infuse the Profaned Flame within his own greatsword, and would perhaps introduce the Profaned Flame to the Fire Witches. They would learn to use its power and summon firestorms with their halberds., and would eventually take Irithyll for themselves.

Sulyvahn would later build a dungeon, and hired some handmaids to guard the prison, which preserves part of the profaned flame in a icy skull.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Yhorm the Giant -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Yhorm, normally spelled Jorm, is an Old Norse word meaning "huge". It appears in the name of the Norse world-serpent *Jormungandr*, literally "huge monster". The spelling Yhorm may help with pronunciation, as the letter J is usually pronounced in Old Norse as a Y.
His appearance seems unique to giants. For one he is the only living giant with facial features, consisting of two bright red eyes and an angular jawline. His proportions are very similar to human proportions, unlike most giants in the games, and he appears to be taller than the giants of Anor Londo.
A player version of Yhorm's armor set exists in the game files, but it is not available to the player under normal circumstances.
Despite being one of the easiest bosses to beat, Yhorm has the highest HP of any boss in *Dark Souls III* (including Darkeater Midir, Sister Friede, and The Demon Prince).

snippet: It is possible to theorize that the event in which the Profaned Flame went out of control, destroying the Profaned Capital, was the result of a Court Sorcerers ritual gone awry. title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After the end of the great war, Lord Gwyn and his clan gained dominion over the world and began their Age of Fire, with the giants continuing to coexist with their civilization in a subordinate but close position. A number of giants became Sentinels guarding the walls and streets of Anor Londo, the city of the gods, employing giant halberds made of brass and retaining the power of lightning, giant shields of white iron, and heavy armor of finely decorated golden brass. An even more powerful group of giants defended the royal cathedral in the center of the city and were capable of performing restorative and offensive miracles.

Gargoyle -  Dark Souls III - enemy - profaned_capital 
 profaned_capital : Gargoyles encountered in the Profaned Capital are often positioned on bridges or rooftops, so the player should be mindful of their surroundings when engaging them in combat. They will disguise themselves as regular statues and will spring to life when in close proximity, although striking them with a ranged weapon will trigger them early. Their attacks inflict Fire damage and they can block attacks with their wings. If struck during this, they will retaliate with a shunt that can send the player flying.

Gargoyles will often take flight and attempt to strike the player from above before crashing down on top of them. By running underneath when they jump, it is possible to sprint past them.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

 dark_souls_iii : By the era of Lothric, when the gods of Anor Londo were but a distant memory, the giants in their employ had been scattered. The Cathedral of the Deep enslaved most of the known surviving giants, forcing them to protect their interests in the Cathedral, Irithyll Dungeon, and occupied Anor Londo. The Giant Sentinels in the city of gods were likely reduced to the disgraced, unclad beasts found sleeping on the way to the old Cathedral of Anor Londo, a line of defense against those intruding on Aldrich. The Greatarchers of Hawkeye Gough went nearly extinct, save one atop a tower in the Undead Settlement who guarded the White Birches found around the foot of the High Wall. Gough himself is remembered for having struck down a calamitous dragon with his Greatbow during the events of *Dark Souls*.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Off to the side is a network of tunnels with multiple holes in the floor, opening up to a caverous, filthy swamp that inflicts Toxic instead of Poison and is occupied by Sewer Centipedes. An old church in visible disarray is half-sunken in the swamp, populated by grotesque hand-headed creatures. A path by the church leads back to Irithyll Dungeon, where one can access otherwise-blocked cells.

On the other side of the chasm and across a half-decimated bridge is a great and ornate façade, flanked by inactive gargoyles. Handmaids surround a golden brazier that perpetually burns, perhaps being the Profaned Flame itself. The entrance is flanked by two antechambers filled with more handmaids, the left one also accessible by the previously-mentioned bridge. Scattered across the whole floor are artifacts of gold and silver, as well as piles of charred, half-melted bodies. Straight ahead is the chamber of Yhorm himself.

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the war dragged on, Vendrick's army began a decline caused by attrition in the face of the Giants' will of steel. The king was forced to hire mercenaries from Forossa and Volgen to reinforce his ranks, and Desert Sorceresses from Jugo were added to the defense of the Royal Castle. The endless battles also began to take their toll on the population. Those who could afford it ran away to other countries while the poor were left without a place to sleep, the kingdom now reduced to ruins. The conflict continued for three generations unabated, with the Giants sustaining their attacks on northern fortifications and trying to push their way inland towards the Royal Castle. The bodies of the many dead giants that littered the region slowly grew into great trees, covering the area around Cardinal Tower in a dense forest.

title: Gravelord Nito
snippet: After the war, while Gwyn developed his civilization of Anor Londo and Izalith that of her namesake city, Nito returned to the depths of the Catacombs, an immense necropolis, to slumber within the Tomb of the Giants, an even deeper place that housed the skeletons of enormous and bestial creatures, and turned the caverns into his domain of light-devouring death. In addition, the deceased members of the race of the Gods of Anor Londo and their priests also rested in the Tombs of the Giants, implying how Nito continued to collaborate with Gwyn by offering the Lord his domain to bury his people and servants. Nito would thus take on the role of administering the death of all manner of beings, giving up much of his Lord Soul into propagating death, earning him the title "Gravelord".

Sometime before the arrival of the Ashen One at the Ringed City, a pygmy—plausibly a disgruntled Pygmy Lord— came to detest the Gods for condemning the pygmies to their accursed fate, and took up residence at the outskirts of their city. title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

snippet:
Giant -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : When fighting a giant, hack away at the legs and dodge any of the giants attacks. This is simple, as their attacks are quite slow. After continuing this rhythm for a short while, eventually the giant will flail around angrily and stomp. This is fairly easy to block with a medium shield and easier to dodge. After the giant has finished its rampage it will crouch down leaving itself defenseless. This is the time that the player should exhaust their entire firepower on the giant.

A safe, although potentially expensive, strategy is to use the Toxic status to kill the Giants. Throwing two Dung Pies at a Giant is enough to apply the effect in NG. After the Toxin takes effect, the player must only wait until the Giant dies.

 appearance : Their heads are largely absent of facial features, apart from a large gaping mouth-like hole at the center. Its function seems to be similar to a mouth, as indicated by the roars that are emanated from within, but Giants have also been known to extract balls of poison and fire from them. Their bodies are covered in a rough, rock-like skin. The upper half of their bodies is generally bulky, with huge protruding shoulders and massive arms, however some are more slender in appearance. They largely wear rudimentary clothing, such as loincloths and ragged robes.

Their brutish appearance and primitive weaponry has led some citizens of Drangleic to view them as being no more than uncivilized barbarians, but contrary evidence shows that they utilize magic and employ concepts such as monarchy and military hierarchy.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - war_with_drangleic 
 war_with_drangleic : Giants are primarily known through their conflict with King Vendrick and his kingdom. According to legend, a mysterious woman named Nashandra, said to be of unparalleled beauty, came to Vendrick long ago and warned him of a looming threat across the seas, in the land of the Giants. King Vendrick named Nashandra his queen and crossed the ocean with her to combat the Giants. During this conflict, he pillaged the Giant's lands, and stole an unspecified "prize", which he brought back to Drangleic. Using this acquired power, Vendrick created various types of Golems, who in turn built Drangleic Castle.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - poison_giant 
 poison_giant : Relatively rare, this type of Giant looks similar to the Melee Giant, but can also throws balls of poison in combat. They wear a hooded robe and their left arm is coated in a green substance, which can poison anything it hits. This type of Giant can be encountered in the Memory of Vammar.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - melee_giant 
 melee_giant : A more common, gray, shorter type of Giant that fights mainly with a large club or fists in battle. They can be encountered in the Memory of Vammar and Orro.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Once the Ashen Mist Heart has been obtained, it can be used to interact with the corpses of three fallen Giants who fought in the war against Vendrick. The heart grants access to the memories of Jeigh, Orro and Vammar. In these memories, the player can witness various battles that took place between the Giants and Vendrick's army. According to Sweet Shalquoir, the Giants savour their memories of glory on the battlefield.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - notes 
 notes : According to concept art and early trailers, Giants were designed with faces, including jagged teeth and possibly even large horns, but these didn't make it into the final game. During the Memory of Jeigh, charred remains of a Giant oddly shows one of these faces.
A plunging attack against the smaller Giant variants will trigger a sync attack that causes the player to stand on their shoulders for several seconds and then strike them directly in the face before stepping off. However this opportunity is rare and can only be performed in several choice areas, due to the relative rarity of Giants.
The Giants are weak to Dark and Magic.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - elite_giant 
 elite_giant : Senior soldiers of the army of Giants. They're typically brown in color and wear a loincloth. They often wield two enormous, obelisk sized stone clubs in combat. Far larger and more formidable than their subordinates, the only Elite Giants to have survived the war reside in a hidden cavern in Black Gulch. They can also be encountered in the Memory of Vammar, Memory of Orro and Memory of Jeigh.

title: Giant Acid Horn Beetle
snippet:
Giant Acid Horn Beetle -  Dark Souls II - enemy - description 
 description : As their name suggests, they are oversized Acid Horn Beetles. The acid clouds they emit can destroy equipment much faster than the normal beetles.

title: Giant Acid Horn Beetle
snippet:

 lead : **Giant Acid Horn Beetles** are enemies in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Giant Acid Horn Beetle
snippet:
Giant Acid Horn Beetle -  Dark Souls II - enemy - location 
 location : One is encountered in the Shrine of Amana, near the Rhoy's Resting Place bonfire.
Another can be found caged in Aldia's Keep.

title: Giant Acid Horn Beetle
snippet:
Giant Acid Horn Beetle -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Like the regular beetles, it is advisable to eliminate them from a distance to avoid equipment breakage. The player can also remove all their equipment and slay the enemies with punches with little risk, as they are unable to fight back.

The giant beetle found in the Shrine of Amana blocks a narrow tunnel and needs to be defeated to proceed.

The caged beetle in Aldia's Keep can be ignored first, as it is unable to break out of confinement. If the player frees all caged creatures by throwing the lever in the adjacent room with the Prowling Magus, the beetle can be killed to get its guaranteed drop.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - locations 
 locations : Undead Settlement
Found at the top of the settlement's tower. To reach him, make the lift that leads to the Road of Sacrifices go down first without riding it, and then ride it up to the top of the tower.
Farron Keep
While not physically reachable in this area, his presence is evidenced by his trademark arrows raining down near the area where the Great Crab attacks in the poisonous swamp.
Cathedral of the Deep
Again, not physically seen here but his arrows will start raining down on the little cemetery located in front of the cathedral's main gates.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Choosing the Young White Branch as a burial gift at the beginning of the game, and carrying it while traversing areas where the Giant Archer attacks, will make him only target enemies.
Young White Branches gifted by the giant have a different in-game description than normal ones and also occupy a different slot within the player's inventory.
**If the player is not carrying one of these particular branches in their inventory, the giant will turn hostile once again.
***Apart from preventing the giant from targeting the player, carrying one of these branches in one's inventory will prevent them from taking any damage from his arrows.
**The giant may be befriended as many times as necessary, presenting the player with another branch each time.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : An unnamed giant reminiscent of Hawkeye Gough. He is similar to those other Giant Slaves found within the Irithyll Dungeon and the Cathedral of the Deep. The shackles he bears and grinds piercing through various parts of his body are evidence of an untold but surely sorrowful past.

A skillful warrior who took refuge on the highest tower of the settlement, now uses his mighty greatbow to defend the land from the monstrosities brought by the curse and which now lurk in this ruined and desolated realm. With astounding accuracy and arrows that explode upon contact, the road leading to meet him will not be an easy one, should one dare to cross his line of fire.

While his monstrous appearance may make one to think it twice before approaching him, once spoken to will reveal he is actually friendly and resolved to provide a helping hand to those who ask for it.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : All three areas where the giant lends a hand are visible from his lookout point at the top of the tower: the Undead Settlement, the Farron Keep, and the Cathedral of the Deep. Those are also the areas where gathering Young White Branches will eventually kill him.
**Likewise, his tower can be seen from all three areas where he helps the player, although it may be difficult to locate it in the Farron Keep due to the dense foliage.
His phrase, "I help anytime." Is the same as that said by the Giant Blacksmith in *Dark Souls*.
The greatbow and greatarrows that he uses are Gough's Greatbow and Gough's Great Arrows, respectively.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:

 lead : The **Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement** is a character in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet: His presence is usually associated with places where young white birches grow. The branches of these trees are thought to be a "token of friendship", which the giant usually presents to those who have gained his trust. Once befriended, he will lend his extraordinary archery skills in some of the most dangerous areas found in Lothric.

title: Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Upon meeting and possibly befriending the giant, the player will have two choices: either let their new friend live to aid them while traversing a few dangerous areas in the game, or kill him to obtain the Hawk Ring.

If the latter option has been chosen, then he may be challenged at the top of his tower in the Undead Settlement; an easy task due to the small space where he is encountered at and which will severely compromise his mobility. In addition, the nearby staircase will provide complete cover from all of his attacks. The giant drops the Hawk Ring upon defeat, an accessory that allows arrows to travel a longer distance.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Giant Blacksmith** is a character in *Dark Souls*. A simple but friendly being, the Giant Blacksmith offers players unique weapon upgrades. He is voiced by Daniel Flynn, who also voiced Solaire of Astora and Vamos.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : It is not recommended to attack him since he is very strong and the services he offers cannot be replaced. However, he is the only character to drop the Blacksmith Giant Hammer, and so must be defeated for completionists. He has the standard Giant moveset.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Little is known about him, aside from his dialogue hinting that he had resided in Anor Londo before most of its denizens left.

The Giant Blacksmith was seemingly on good terms with Hawkeye Gough. This is hinted at with the Hawk Ring found in a chest next to him, as well as Gough's friendly remarks about the Giant Blacksmith.

His corpse is found in *Dark Souls III* in Anor Londo, on the same spot he used to reside. The Giant's Coal is found at his body.

Andre of Astora apparently knew him, as he says "*I miss the old bugger, I do.*" when given the Giant's Coal. He also assumes that the Giant Blacksmith had passed a long time ago.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : Located in the corner next to him is a chest containing the Hawk Ring. It is not necessary to kill him to access it; rolling right behind him should suffice.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : The Giant Blacksmith sells a variety of useful upgrade materials as well as weapons and armor, and is the only blacksmith that can upgrade down the lightning path (by default), the crystal path (after he receives the Crystal Ember), and make weapons from the souls of bosses. Many of the things he sells are exclusive only to him, such as Twinkling Titanite and Dragonslayer Arrows.

title: Giant Blacksmith
snippet:
Giant Blacksmith -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : In Anor Londo after rotating the bridge between the Bell Gargoyles, ascend some steps towards a large building guarded by two Sentinels and several Batwing Demons. The door on the left leads towards the Giant Blacksmith, but initially it is locked and can only be opened from the other side, which can be accessed only after clearing most of Anor Londo.

Remember to open the locked door leading back to the Sentinels, so it is easier to access the blacksmith from the other bonfire.

snippet:
Giant Clam -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Giant Clams are an easy source of Twinkling Titanite, an otherwise expensive upgrade material. They can be farmed in Ash Lake and the Crystal Cave, where they can be respawned repeatedly.
Shooting an arrow into a Giant Clam's mouth will briefly stun it.
When encountering Seath the Scaleless for the first time, in the Crystal Cave, the fog wall is not present. This allows the clams the chance to enter the room that houses the boss fight, if the player tries to run past them. Seath's attacks can harm them, but they will still only attack the player, making the fight a fair bit more challenging.

title: Giant Crow
snippet:
Giant Crow -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Giant Crow** is a minor character in *Dark Souls* and can be found in Firelink Shrine throughout all of the story.

title: Giant Crow
snippet:
Giant Crow -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : Attacking the Crow enough will prompt it to fly away, however it will return and continue to transport the Chosen Undead. It is impossible to kill the Giant Crow without mods. However, using mods to kill the Crow yields 5,000 souls. The crow also has no death animation.
After flying away it will still transport the Chosen Undead to the Asylum even if it hasn't returned yet.
The Crestfallen Warrior makes mention of the Giant Crow lifting a man, curled up in a ball, in its clutches and carrying him off, as a hint for Undead Asylum Revisited

title: Giant Crow
snippet:
Giant Crow -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : The Giant Crow is a mysterious entity that transports the Chosen Undead from the end of the Undead Asylum to Firelink Shrine in Lordran.

Once the elevator is operated in the Undead Parish Church it is possible to revisit the Undead Asylum by climbing to the top of the ruins in Firelink Shrine to the Giant Crow's nest and curling up into a ball. The Giant Crow will then bring the Chosen Undead onto another nest on the cliff where the player was first carried off from in the Undead Asylum.

Beyond this, no further interaction can be made with the Crow.

The crow can actually be shot at but will fly away upon reaching half health

title: Giant Door Shield
snippet:
Giant Door Shield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description

Heirlooms of the knight who was known as the protector of the meek, yet who failed to protect anyone.

Skill: Lockout
Get a stalwart defense, and shield bash, or strong attack for a heave that holds shields to block nearly all damage.

title: Giant Door Shield
snippet:
Giant Door Shield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Perhaps the most unconventional weapon in *Dark Souls III*, the Giant Door Shields are towering titans that grant strong defensive power with its attacks.

While classified as paired greatshields, these shields function more akin to fist weapons, albeit significantly slower. The greatshields perform bashing attacks using the shields as weapons. Unlike normal shields that have limited attacks to back their strictly defensive purpose, the Giant Door Shields possess a robust if short-ranged moveset that allows the wielder to fight offensively with a truly unique playstyle.

title: Giant Door Shield
snippet:
Giant Door Shield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - upgrades 
 upgrades : Reinforced with Titanite.

title: Giant Door Shield
snippet:
What makes the Giant Door Shields so powerful is their ability to utilize block frames (similar to Valorheart) and Hyper Armor during attacks, which also cannot be parried under any circumstances due to their nature as ultra weapons. This means that by taking advantage of Poise, the Giant Door Shields are extremely difficult to interrupt once in motion, and most physical attacks will be easily shrugged off by the weapon's block frames.

Of course, all these strengths come at a steep price. The Door Shields have an extremely high Strength requirement, demand heavy Vitality investment to support their weight, and consume extreme amounts of stamina to attack and to block, forcing the wielder to invest in Endurance. As well, their wooden nature makes them quite vulnerable to Fire damage, which can only be protected against by utilizing its skill.
